Name of the Surah

• It is called al-Kawthar (Abundance), because it opens with mention of al-Kawthar, which means abundant good, and from which comes the name of a river in Paradise.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• The good news to the Prophet (ﷺ) that he is given the river al-Kawthar, a special blessing bestowed on him alone, which no one else has been given; and his (ﷺ) being commanded to thank Allah for it by devoting himself to His worship, Allah's defence of him (ﷺ), and His repelling of his enemies.

[The Tafsir]

Indeed, We have given you, O Prophet, abundant good in this world and the Hereafter, and among it is the river al-Kawthar in Paradise, whose banks are tents of hollow pearls, and whose clay is musk.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 108, verse 2:

So devote your prayer entirely to your Lord, and sacrifice your offering to Him alone, invoking only His name.

The commentary on Surah 108, verse 3:

"Indeed, the one who hates you and what you have brought of guidance and light is the one whose trace is cut off, cut off from every good."
